parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Electric current is a flow of charge carriers. The charge on the carriers is quantised. Explain what is meant by *quantised*.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
A battery of electromotive force (e.m.f.) $9.0\text{ V}$ and internal resistance $0.25\ \Omega$ is connected in series with two identical resistors X and a resistor Y, as shown in Fig. 7.1.

{{figure:figure_7_1}}

Fig. 7.1

The resistance of each resistor X is $0.15\ \Omega$ and the resistance of resistor Y is $2.7\ \Omega$.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Show that the current in the circuit is $2.8\text{ A}$.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Calculate the potential difference across the battery.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Each resistor X connected in the circuit in (b) is made from a wire with a cross-sectional area of $2.5\text{ mm}^2$. The number of free electrons per unit volume in the wire is $8.5 \times 10^{29}\text{ m}^{-3}$.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: Calculate the average drift speed of the electrons in X.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
The two resistors X are replaced by two resistors Z made of the same material and length but with half the diameter.

Describe and explain the difference between the average drift speed in Z and that in X.
